sonido/33f18da:
Five foundational signal processing modules that round out sonido-analysis
as a general-purpose DSP toolkit beyond its existing spectral analysis:

- LMS/NLMS adaptive filters for noise cancellation, echo cancellation,
  and system identification (Haykin ch. 5-6)
- Cross-correlation with direct O(n·max_lag) and FFT-based O(n·log·n)
  implementations, normalized variant, and signed peak lag detection
  (Oppenheim & Schafer §2.8)
- Digital down-conversion: NCO + anti-aliasing FIR + integer decimation
  for shifting bandpass signals to complex baseband (Lyons ch. 10)
- Phase unwrapping extracted from transfer_fn.rs and hilbert.rs into a
  standalone module with configurable tolerance, quality-guided
  unwrapping (variance-based seed selection), and streaming PhaseTracker
  (Ghiglia & Pritt ch. 3)
- Rational resampling via polyphase filter decomposition — decimate,
  interpolate, and arbitrary P/Q rate conversion without explicit
  zero-insertion (Vaidyanathan ch. 4)

No new deps — rustfft covers FFT-based xcorr and DDC complex mixing.
30 new tests (126 total unit + 22 integration + 8 doc-tests).

two-top/336027f:
Short vibration one-shots on the punchy beats — your throw (10 ms), a kill
(60 ms), your perfect catch (15 ms) — off the same Local prev-state edges the
audio/effect systems use.

- crates/app/src/haptics.rs: HapticsPlugin. The `vibrate` leaf is a JNI hop
  to the platform Vibrator on Android (activity handle via ndk_context →
  attach JVM → getSystemService("vibrator") → vibrate(long), the API-24-safe
  overload; any JNI error is logged + swallowed, never crashes the loop), and
  a no-op on every other target — so the three detector systems are identical
  cross-platform and only the leaf differs. Lives in `app` for the same reason
  audio does: a vibrator is a device.
- Throw and perfect-catch are your-action feedback → gated to the local
  player via a new `LocalPlayerHandle(Option<usize>)` resource (netplay sets
  it from the peer-agreed handle in perform_swap; `None` in couch/SyncTest
  where both players share the device → every handle counts as local). A kill
  is a round-defining impact and fires for either player. The resource is
  reusable — the match-summary banner (5.5) will want "you" vs "them" too.
- Android-only target deps `jni`/`ndk-context`, pinned to the copies already
  in the lock (no new crate versions).

Verification: the desktop no-op path + the local-filter logic are covered by
the gate (354 tests, clippy --all-targets clean). The Android JNI surface was
type-checked in isolation against jni 0.21.1 + ndk-context 0.1.1 via
`cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android` (it compiles) — the full APK
build + on-device feel stay operator-batched (M6), matching the matrix's
existing `--exclude app` on Android. No sim change → no sync_test/canonical.
